solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Break the French ram (3-2)

blocks.note: a tup is a ram, a British farming word

annotation.surface: A French ram breaks out of its field.
annotation.walkthrough: TUP is the British farmers' word for a ram, common in crosswords and worth learning.
annotation.definitionFit: A let-up is a pause or break in something unpleasant, like rain.

entries.clue: Renaissance man playing odd arcane violin (8,2,5)

indicatorNotes.playing: the letters are played about with, like notes on an instrument

annotation.surface: A man of the Renaissance performs on a strange, mysterious violin.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface hands you a musician, and 'Renaissance man' reads as any versatile genius; it is the original one.
annotation.definitionFit: Leonardo da Vinci is the archetypal Renaissance man, painter, engineer and inventor at once.

entries.clue: Opponents of US with American motif (5)

blocks.note: us and them: the other side

annotation.surface: America's enemies adopt an American design.
annotation.walkthrough: 'US' in capitals looks like the country, but it is just 'us', whose opposite is 'them'.
annotation.definitionFit: A thema is a theme or subject, a motif in music or argument.

entries.clue: Supply large amount of blood for Halloween staple (7)

blocks.note: to pump money or water in is to supply lots of it

annotation.surface: Buckets of fake blood are needed for Halloween.
annotation.walkthrough: The gore of the surface is misdirection: 'blood' means relatives, as in 'blood is thicker than water'.
annotation.definitionFit: Carved pumpkins are an essential part of Halloween.

entries.clue: Tossing Crime and Punishment, not working hard (9)

indicatorNotes.Tossing: the letters of CRIME are tossed about
indicatorNotes.not working: ON means working, so 'not working' removes ON

blocks.note: LESSON (a punishment, as in 'teach them a lesson') without ON

annotation.surface: Someone gives up on reading Dostoevsky's hefty novel because it is too much like hard work.
annotation.walkthrough: The novel's title is split in two: 'and' just joins the halves. 'Hard' at the end looks like part of 'not working hard'.
annotation.definitionFit: Merciless means hard, showing no pity.

entries.clue: Hybrid shoe (4)

blocks.note: a hybrid animal: the offspring of a donkey and a horse

annotation.surface: A shoe that combines two styles.
annotation.walkthrough: Read together, the words suggest a trainer-sandal crossover; apart, they are an animal and a slipper.
annotation.definitionFit: Mule names both the donkey-horse cross and a backless shoe.

entries.clue: Weak creature, he’s to what extent to be in charge? (3,3,4)

blocks.note: the runt is the weakest of a litter

annotation.surface: Someone asks how far a feeble person can be put in charge.
annotation.walkthrough: The word breaks fall in different places: RUNT HES HOW regroups as RUN THE SHOW.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom from the theatre: whoever runs the show is in charge, and the phrase stretches to any organisation.

entries.clue: Goad that is pressing fairly soft part of elephant briefly (7)

indicatorNotes.pressing: IE presses round MP, holding it
indicatorNotes.briefly: TUSK is cut short by its last letter

blocks.note: mp = mezzo piano, the musical marking for fairly soft

annotation.surface: A mahout prods an elephant gently on a tender spot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fairly soft' sounds like a description of the elephant's skin; it is a musical dynamic.
annotation.definitionFit: An impetus is a driving force, something that goads you on.

entries.clue: Best opera wants you observing each part’s body language (9)

indicatorNotes.observing each part’s body: take the body, the inside, of each word

annotation.surface: A singer is told the best operas need attention to every part of the performer's body language.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Body language' reads as one phrase, but 'body' belongs to the wordplay: the bodies of four words, stripped of their first and last letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain example: Esperanto is an invented tongue, built in the 1880s for international use.

entries.clue: Receive me, mostly exercising ability to forget inconvenient things (9,6)

indicatorNotes.exercising: the letters are put through their paces, moved about

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 15 letters; 'mostly' is part of it

annotation.surface: Someone asks to be welcomed, mainly while at the gym.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' looks like an instruction to shorten something, but it is fodder: its letters supply S, L, T, M, O and Y.
annotation.definitionFit: Selective memory is remembering what suits you and forgetting what is awkward.

entries.clue: Fruit and honey seen in High Noon, eg (4,5)

indicatorNotes.seen in: MEL is seen inside the other letters
indicatorNotes.High: high = intoxicated, so the letters are in a wild state

blocks.note: NOON EG, rearranged, split around the honey
mel is Latin for honey, as in mellifluous

annotation.surface: A cowboy snacks on fruit and honey while watching the western High Noon.
annotation.walkthrough: High Noon is a famous western, but 'High' is just the anagram signal, like 'stoned' or 'drunk'. MEL for honey is a crossword standard.
annotation.definitionFit: An Ogen melon is a small sweet melon variety developed in Israel.

entries.clue: Reject relish from a development stage (5)

indicatorNotes.Reject: to reject is to throw back, turning the letters round

blocks.note: to lap up something is to relish it

annotation.surface: Someone spurns a condiment that is still being developed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Relish' looks like a pickle, but it is the verb: to lap up, to enjoy greedily.
annotation.definitionFit: Pupal describes the pupa, the stage between larva and adult insect.

entries.clue: Disconnected state after Jamaican music (6)

blocks.note: à la = after the manner of
ska is a Jamaican forerunner of reggae

annotation.surface: A mood of disconnection follows listening to reggae.
annotation.walkthrough: 'After' looks like a position instruction; it is À LA, as in 'after the style of'. Alaska is disconnected from the other mainland states by Canada.
annotation.definitionFit: Alaska is the US state cut off from the rest by Canada.

entries.clue: Butler in fiction, not quite 17, disregarding duke’s bombast (8)

indicatorNotes.disregarding: to disregard something is to leave it out of account, so the D for duke is dropped from DORIC

blocks.note: RHETT Butler of Gone with the Wind, minus his last letter
DORIC (the answer to 17 across) without D for duke

annotation.surface: A butler in a novel, not yet seventeen, ignores a duke's pompous talk.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Butler' suggests a servant like Jeeves; it is Rhett Butler's surname. D = duke is a standard abbreviation.
annotation.definitionFit: Rhetoric can mean inflated, showy language, i.e. bombast.

entries.clue: Dull radio presenter on outside broadcast where promotion will be missed (4-3,3)

blocks.note: to dull a sound or pain is to deaden it
OB = outside broadcast, a BBC term

annotation.surface: A boring radio host out on location is passed over for promotion.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dull' reads as an adjective describing the presenter, but it is the verb deaden.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: a dead end goes nowhere, so a job with that label offers no route upwards.

entries.clue: Puts off securing vessel or vessels (9)

indicatorNotes.securing: DETERS secures CAN by holding it inside

blocks.note: to deter is to put off

annotation.surface: Someone delays tying up a boat, or several boats.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' in the surface means a ship, and the second 'vessels' seems to repeat it; both are containers.
annotation.definitionFit: Decanters are glass vessels for serving wine.

entries.clue: Irish can’t reform Catholic? (9)

indicatorNotes.reform: the letters are formed again in a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters; the apostrophe is ignored

annotation.surface: An Irish Catholic declines to become a Protestant.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Reform' calls up the Reformation, the very thing an Irish Catholic might refuse. The question mark flags Catholic as one example of a Christian.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example, flagged by the question mark: Catholics are one branch of the church that follows Jesus.

entries.clue: Non-human intelligence on transgressions against God, here? (5)

blocks.note: sin, taken as a mass noun

annotation.surface: A robot lectures about sins against God.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by place: the mountain where Moses was given the commandments, the rules against wrongdoing.
annotation.definitionFit: Mount Sinai is where Moses received the Ten Commandments, the rules against sin.

entries.clue: Ancient dialect of US capital taking over Rhode Island (5)

indicatorNotes.taking: DC takes the other letters inside

blocks.note: R and I, the first letters of Rhode Island

annotation.surface: The old way of speaking in Washington spreads to Rhode Island.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Over' looks like part of 'taking over'; it is O, the cricket abbreviation. An over is a set of six balls bowled.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain example: this was one of the main dialect groups of ancient Greek, spoken in Sparta.

entries.clue: Dish of food left on the counter (7)

indicatorNotes.on the counter: counter = contrary, running the other way

annotation.surface: A plate of food has been left out on the kitchen counter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Left' and 'counter' both look like kitchen words; one is a political colour and the other means backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a thick New England soup of clams or fish, served as a dish.

entries.clue: Declines ice cream cake (4,5)

annotation.surface: Someone turns down an ice cream cake.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Declines' reads as refuses; it is falls. A drop scone is a small thick pancake, also called a Scotch pancake.
annotation.definitionFit: A drop scone is a small griddle cake made by dropping batter onto a hot pan.

entries.clue: Maybe Pet Sounds’ first poster includes Mike Love predominantly, yes? (7)

indicatorNotes.first: take the first letter of Sounds
indicatorNotes.includes: AD includes the letters between its own
indicatorNotes.predominantly: most of YES, without its last letter

blocks.note: Mike is M in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A Beach Boys fan asks whether the first Pet Sounds poster features Mike Love most prominently.
annotation.walkthrough: Pet Sounds is the Beach Boys album and Mike Love their singer, so 'Pet' looks locked into the title. It is the definition: a Samoyed is one kind of pet.
annotation.definitionFit: A Samoyed is a fluffy white Siberian dog breed, so maybe a pet.

entries.clue: Noble verse that’s followed by “lives matter” (8)

blocks.note: v = verse, as in Bible references

annotation.surface: A poem whose next line is the protest slogan 'lives matter'.
annotation.walkthrough: The quotation points to the Black Lives Matter slogan; here 'matter' just means count.
annotation.definitionFit: A viscount is a nobleman ranking between earl and baron.

entries.clue: Stick with announcement from someone who’s 23 (6)

blocks.note: a person announcing their own state begins 'I am', shortened
the answer to 23 down, ASHEN, means this: grey-faced

annotation.surface: Someone who has gone grey sticks to their story.
annotation.walkthrough: The cross-reference sends you to ASHEN; a person who is ashen announces 'I'm pale'.
annotation.definitionFit: To impale is to stick something through with a point.

entries.clue: Grey arsenic in that case, unopened (5)

blocks.note: As is the chemical symbol for arsenic
THEN (in that case) without its first letter

annotation.surface: A grey poison is found in a case that has never been opened.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In that case' looks like a place to find the arsenic, but it is THEN, as in 'then we'll go'.
annotation.definitionFit: Ashen means pale grey, the colour of ash.

entries.clue: Nancy’s friend Oliver perhaps avoiding leader (4)

indicatorNotes.avoiding leader: JAMIE goes without his first letter

blocks.note: Jamie Oliver, the British TV chef

annotation.surface: Nancy's friend Oliver is keeping out of the boss's way.
annotation.walkthrough: Nancy looks like a person, but it is the French city, so her friend is French: amie. Oliver is Jamie Oliver, the British celebrity chef.
annotation.definitionFit: Amie is French for a female friend, as said in Nancy.

entries.clue: Spirit that’s invalid and regularly ignored (5)

indicatorNotes.regularly ignored: every other letter is ignored, leaving the rest

blocks.note: iNvAlId AnD: I, V, L, D, A ignored

annotation.surface: A ghost that is sick and overlooked by everyone.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Invalid' reads as a sick person; only its letters matter here.
annotation.definitionFit: A naiad is a water nymph, a spirit of rivers and springs in Greek myth.

entries.clue: Fashion designer – male, unknown in Scotland – choosing to leave shop (5,4)

indicatorNotes.to leave: to leave is to go away, so SING departs from inside CHOOSING

blocks.note: in Scotland a man whose name you don't know is addressed as Jimmy
CHOOSING without SING; to shop someone is to inform on them, to sing

annotation.surface: A designer boutique owner picks the day to close the shop.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shop' looks like the store; it is the British slang verb meaning to betray to the police, which is also 'sing'.
annotation.definitionFit: Jimmy Choo is a Malaysian-born fashion designer famous for his shoes.

entries.clue: Unimportant artist entering base (9)

indicatorNotes.entering: to enter is to go into, so RA goes into the middle of IGNOBLE

annotation.surface: A minor painter joins an army base.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Base' reads as a camp or foundation; it is the adjective meaning dishonourable. RA is the standard crossword artist.
annotation.definitionFit: Something ignorable is unimportant enough to be ignored.

entries.clue: Beau Bridges acted — and yet … (5)

indicatorNotes.Bridges: the answer bridges three words, spanning the gaps between them

annotation.surface: A grudging review of the actor Beau Bridges' performance.
annotation.walkthrough: Beau Bridges is an American actor, so the first two words look like a name; 'Beau' is the definition and 'Bridges' the signal.
annotation.definitionFit: A beau, like Beau Brummell, is a dandy, a man devoted to fine clothes.
